completedWork: REWORK 2 after the phase B re-review (security findings). SEC-B-2: openDb now sets PRAGMA recursive_triggers = ON inside the retry-protected pragmas, so REPLACE conflict resolution fires the DELETE triggers; no migration change. Three SEC-B-2 tests in test/unit/db/triggers.test.js (REPLACE per table refused, rows unchanged; plain and INSERT OR IGNORE inserts still work). Reproduced first (ev:ev-mv1ilouz-013ab82a, three REPRO lines), then the same probe passes with no-repro lines and the control (ev:ev-mv1iobfp-016ca5a4). SEC-B-3: readJsonBody scans the text without recursion and refuses nesting deeper than 32 levels with 422 VALIDATION_FAILED, details.fields [{field body, rule depth:32}]; canonicalJson also refuses input nested deeper than 32 with a TypeError instead of overflowing the stack. Tests in test/unit/http/hardening.test.js (SEC-B-3: 20,000-deep body, 32 accepted and 33 refused, brackets in strings, canonicalJson). Reproduced first with the reviewer's http probe (ev:ev-mv1ilp8t-017fc2a5, status 200 and fingerprint throws RangeError); verified with .eccode/drafts/b1-secb3-verify.mjs, the same scenario expecting 422 and a healthy server (ev:ev-mv1iobpi-01402abf). The reviewer's probe itself now reports one FAIL, because its section H expectation encodes the bug (it expects the body to be accepted); that is the fix working. SEC-B-4 (taken, cheap): createHttpServer sets connectionsCheckingInterval 1000 so the 10 s and 30 s timeouts fire on time, maxConnections 512, and answers ERR_HTTP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT with 408 instead of 400; tests SEC-B-4 in hardening.test.js use short timeouts. SEC-B-5 (taken): ensureRuntimeDirs tightens an existing directory named data or uploads, owned by the current user, to 0700; other existing directories are left alone; test in startup.test.js. For b4's README: an existing data/ is now tightened to 0700 at start, and the backup line should say to run it under umask 077. Declared verification command passes with 188 tests (ev:ev-mv1iol67-014cd738); npm test passes 381/381 (ev:ev-mv1iox8y-01e625bf). EARLIER REWORK after phase B review rev-mv1hc5zg-01a3fc75. PB-1 (blocking), root cause: on a fresh database file, PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL needs an exclusive lock. When another process holds or awaits a write lock while this connection holds a shared one, waiting could deadlock, so SQLite returns SQLITE_BUSY immediately and never calls the busy handler, so busy_timeout does not help. Reproduced with the reviewer's script (ev:ev-mv1hf138-016b38f3: 3 of 40 sequential runs failed with 'database is locked'; the script always exits 0, so the counts are the result) and with a minimal probe (.eccode/drafts/b1-pb1-probe.mjs, error code 5 from the WAL switch, about 1 in 180 opens). Fix in src/db/connection.js: openDb reads the journal mode first and switches only when the file is not WAL, and both that step and the later pragmas run under retryWhileBusy, a bounded back-off (2 ms doubling to 50 ms with jitter) on SQLITE_BUSY/LOCKED up to max(busyTimeoutMs, 1000 ms), after which the busy error is rethrown; the handle is closed on failure. New test/unit/db/open-race.test.js (all named PB-1): retry unit tests, bounded give-up against a real lock-holder process, success when the holder releases, and a stress of 25 rounds x 4 processes on a fresh file. The same reproduction command now shows 0 failures in 160 runs (ev:ev-mv1hidob-01eb30b6); six more stress runs also passed; npm test passes 370/370 (ev:ev-mv1hjizn-013960db); the declared verification command passes with 177 tests (ev:ev-mv1hj5be-01ed33dd). PB-2: six tests renamed with ARCH-26, SEC-10, SEC-12, SEC-3 (RS_TEST_HOOKS row), RS-14 and ARCH-25. Original work: Wrote package.json first (type module, engines >=22.13, zero dependencies, devDependency @playwright/test 1.56.1, the nine scripts of Testing Strategy > Commands verbatim). Tests: 171 across test/unit/config, db, http and seed, including the eight files named in the verification command. The final run of the task command, recorded as the declared command string (ev:ev-mv1g9bkw-01abf3c8, also ev:ev-mv1g7ma5-01bc9fb8 wrapped in sh -c), passed with 171 tests and the same tests also pass under a loopback-only network guard at concurrency 4 (ev:ev-mv1g7yel-017eb8cd). remainingIssues: Not done, outside b1 or a later task: SEC-B-1 and SEC-B-8 (domain, b2), SEC-B-9 (c1 must validate the X-Forwarded-For entry with net.isIP before using it as a throttle key), SEC-B-6 (no package-lock.json committed; a decision for the orchestrator/b4), SEC-B-7 (scrypt N is a one-constant change in scripts/seed.js that c1's verifier must then match).

SEC-B-4 residual: the reviewer saw one unexplained slow-header connection still open at 50 s after a long probe sequence. With the 1 s check interval the timeouts now fire on time in my tests, but I did not re-run the reviewer's --slowloris probe or isolate that case.
maxConnections is 512, a value I chose (the spec names none); a deployment behind a proxy with more concurrent connections would need it raised.
The reviewer's race script tr-phb-migrate-race.mjs always exits 0, so its pass/fail is read from the printed counts (0 failed in the PB-1 verification run), not from the exit code.

openDb now waits up to max(busy_timeout, 1000 ms) at open time even when RS_DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS=0, because the WAL switch happens once per process at startup; ordinary statements still honour the configured timeout.

Upload timeout: the spec gives uploads 60 s, but Node has one server-wide requestTimeout. server.js sets 30 s and exports UPLOAD_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS; task d3 (upload route) must enforce its own 60 s deadline while streaming, or change the server value deliberately.

Password hash format is defined here (scripts/seed.js hashPassword): scrypt$16384$8$1$<salt base64url>$<64-byte key base64url>. Task c1 (src/auth/password.js) must verify exactly this format, since c1 does not own the seed; the dummy hash for unknown users must use the same parameters.

Config refuses placeholder-shaped values for every secret it reads (SEC-5, literal reading of the spec), including unused PayPal and Anthropic ones. A .env.example copied verbatim with <placeholder> values therefore fails startup and seed, naming the variable. Task b4 should ship .env.example with those lines commented out or explain it in the README.

Two AppError classes exist: src/domain/errors.js (b2, constructor (status, code, message, details)) and src/http/envelope.js. The HTTP layer adopts the domain one by duck typing (name AppError, status 400-599, code in the catalog), answering with the catalog message and only plain-object details; the envelope class also accepts the domain-style argument order. A domain error with a code outside the catalog becomes 500 INTERNAL by design.

The router requires a policy on every route and non-public policies are denied with 401 until task c1 passes an authorize hook to createApp (and adds the Origin/CSRF checks, session cookie handling and rate limits, none of which are in b1).

main.js starts only the HTTP server. The fake approval listener, reconciler and retention sweep are added by e1, e4 and d3. The model-provider fallback to fake when the claude binary is absent is left to d1/d3; config only forces fake under RS_TEST_OFFLINE=1.

config.publicUrl is null when RS_PUBLIC_URL is unset (PORT=0 has no port yet). Code needing the app origin must call deps.publicUrl() (http://localhost:<bound port> by default). The log allow-list has one addition to the spec list: port, needed for the harness 'listening' line.

scripts/seed.js embeds RS-FIX-1 as a constant; it was not cross-checked against test/fixtures/rs-fix-1.json (b2's file) because that file was not part of this task. The seed test asserts the brief table values.

The loopback-only guard used in ev:ev-mv1g7yel-017eb8cd is a scratch stand-in (.eccode/drafts/b1-net-guard.mjs) because test/helpers/net-guard.js belongs to b3; re-run these tests under the real guard once it exists.
The ES5 property of check-node.cjs is checked by a regex scan plus real runs on Node 20 and 21, not by an ES5 parser.
